os-pkgs-ubuntu.Title: GnuPG: GnuPG: Information disclosure and potential arbitrary code execution via out-of-bounds write
os-pkgs-ubuntu.Description: In GnuPG before 2.4.9, armor_filter in g10/armor.c has two increments of an index variable where one is intended, leading to an out-of-bounds write for crafted input. (For ExtendedLTS, 2.2.51 and later are fixed versions.)

os-pkgs-ubuntu.Title: kernel: KVM: arm64: Tear down vGIC on failed vCPU creation
os-pkgs-ubuntu.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: arm64: Tear down vGIC on failed vCPU creation

If kvm_arch_vcpu_create() fails to share the vCPU page with the
hypervisor, we propagate the error back to the ioctl but leave the
vGIC vCPU data initialised. Note only does this leak the corresponding
memory when the vCPU is destroyed but it can also lead to use-after-free
if the redistributor device handling tries to walk into the vCPU.

Add the missing cleanup to kvm_arch_vcpu_create(), ensuring that the
vGIC vCPU structures are destroyed on error.

os-pkgs-ubuntu.Title: kernel: ksmbd: fix Preauh_HashValue race condition
os-pkgs-ubuntu.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix Preauh_HashValue race condition

If client send multiple session setup requests to ksmbd,
Preauh_HashValue race condition could happen.
There is no need to free sess->Preauh_HashValue at session setup phase.
It can be freed together with session at connection termination phase.

os-pkgs-ubuntu.Title: kernel: net: appletalk: Fix use-after-free in AARP proxy probe

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: appletalk: Fix use-after-free in AARP proxy probe

The AARP proxy‐probe routine (aarp_proxy_probe_network) sends a probe,
releases the aarp_lock, sleeps, then re-acquires the lock.  During that
window an expire timer thread (__aarp_expire_timer) can remove and
kfree() the same entry, leading to a use-after-free.

race condition:

         cpu 0                          |            cpu 1
    atalk_sendmsg()                     |   atif_proxy_probe_device()
    aarp_send_ddp()                     |   aarp_proxy_probe_network()
    mod_timer()                         |   lock(aarp_lock) // LOCK!!
    timeout around 200ms                |   alloc(aarp_entry)
    and then call                       |   proxies[hash] = aarp_entry
    aarp_expire_timeout()               |   aarp_send_probe()
                                        |   unlock(aarp_lock) // UNLOCK!!
    lock(aarp_lock) // LOCK!!           |   msleep(100);
    __aarp_expire_timer(&proxies[ct])   |
    free(aarp_entry)                    |
    unlock(aarp_lock) // UNLOCK!!       |
                                        |   lock(aarp_lock) // LOCK!!
                                        |   UAF aarp_entry !!

os-pkgs-ubuntu.Title: kernel: io_uring/futex: ensure io_futex_wait() cleans up properly on failure
os-pkgs-ubuntu.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/futex: ensure io_futex_wait() cleans up properly on failure

The io_futex_data is allocated upfront and assigned to the io_kiocb
async_data field, but the request isn't marked with REQ_F_ASYNC_DATA
at that point. Those two should always go together, as the flag tells
io_uring whether the field is valid or not.

Additionally, on failure cleanup, the futex handler frees the data but
does not clear ->async_data. Clear the data and the flag in the error
path as well.

Thanks to Trend Micro Zero Day Initiative and particularly ReDress for
reporting this.

shortDescription:
MoSBi (Molecular Signature identification using Biclustering) is a comprehensive
        framework for identifying biclusters in molecular data. It uses multiple biclustering
        algorithms and provides robust methods for evaluating and visualizing the results.
longDescription:
# MoSBi: Molecular Signature Identification using Biclustering
## Overview

**MoSBi** (Molecular Signature Identification from Biclustering) is an ensemble-based biclustering framework tailored for molecular omics data. It standardizes the output of various biclustering algorithms and merges their results to compute robust **ensemble biclusters**.

MoSBi constructs **similarity networks** of biclusters across algorithms, filters them using a custom **error model**, and applies **Louvain modularity** to extract bicluster communities. These communities can then be interpreted as stable molecular signatures.

Additionally, MoSBi includes network visualization tools that offer an intuitive and scalable representation of results.

---

## Key Features

- Unified interface for biclustering results
- Multi-algorithm ensemble computation
- Similarity network construction and filtering
- Louvain-based community detection
- Visualization of results with heatmaps and network plots
- Easily extensible to new biclustering algorithms

---

## Configuration

### Hyperparameters

| Name               | Type       | Default     | Description                                                                 |
|--------------------|------------|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `n_randomizations` | INTEGER    | `'5'`       | Number of randomizations for cut-off estimation                             |
| `margin`           | CATEGORICAL| `both`      | Margin for similarity computation (`row`, `column`, `mean`, `both`)         |
| `metric`           | CATEGORICAL| `Bray-Curtis` | Similarity metric (`Bray-Curtis`, `Jaccard`, `Overlap Coefficient`, `Fowlkes-Mallows`) |
| `n_steps`          | INTEGER    | `'100'`     | Number of points where the cut-off is evaluated                             |
| `sn_ratio`         | BOOLEAN    | `'true'`    | Compute signal-to-noise ratio if `true`, else use error threshold           |

---

### Input

| Name  | Type | Description | Required |
|--------|------|-------------|----------|
| `data` | CSV  | TSV file     | `false`  |

---

### Output

| Name                 | Type   | Description              |
|----------------------|--------|--------------------------|
| `adjacency_heatmap`  | STRING | Adjacency heatmap file   |
| `histograms`         | STRING | Histogram visualizations |
| `network_by_algorithm` | STRING | Network structure by algorithm |
| `network_plot`       | STRING | Final network plot       |

---

## More

You can find all information at:

🔗 **[Tool](https://exbio.wzw.tum.de/mosbi/)**
